title: First Upgrade Price by Segment Length — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand
content:
**Tariff clause — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** The First upgrade charge is the fare brand's First upgrade price for that segment, the short-segment price when the segment distance recorded on the segment's seat entry is at most the segment length threshold and the long-segment price otherwise. The charge is stated to the cent.

## Terms

- **That segment.** The ticket's first unflown segment: the segment whose number is one more than the number of coupons already flown on the ticket.
- **Segment distance.** The statute miles recorded on the latest seat entry of that segment.
- **The fare brand's First upgrade price.** The short-segment and long-segment prices for an upgrade into First, and the segment length threshold, as the fare brand's paid upgrade price list and seat fee schedule give them.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Coupons flown | Segment upgraded | Distance on the seat entry against the threshold | Charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Segment 1 | At most the threshold (equal counts) | Short-segment First upgrade price |
| 1 | Segment 2 | Above the threshold | Long-segment First upgrade price |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Suppose a fare brand listed an upgrade into First at 140 dollars short and 310 dollars long with a threshold of 1000 miles. A ticket with one flown coupon has segment 2 as its first unflown segment; that segment's seat entry records 1,480 miles, so the First upgrade charge is 310.00 dollars. Had the entry recorded 1,000 miles, the charge would be 140.00 dollars.
